name: Hazaragi (Afghan Dari, Hazara)

ancestors.notes: Mongolic substrate from the Mongol-Turkic settlement of Hazarajat (~13th c.): residual vocabulary and the prominence of uvular/velar-nasal segments described by Dulling 1973 and Efimov 1965.

notes: Hazaragi (هزارگی). Dari dialect of Hazara people of central Afghanistan (Hazarajat). Hazara descend from Mongol-Turkic settlers (~13th c. CE) who adopted Dari but retain Mongolian substrate features. /q/ and /ɢ/ prominent; /ŋ/ phonemic in Mongolian loanwords. Some uvular vowel features. Spoken by ~2–3 million people; large diaspora in Iran, Pakistan, and internationally. Already-encoded allophones confirmed against the cited sources: ق prefers the uvular stop [q] with [ɢ] as a prominent variant (Dulling 1973); nasal /n/ carries [ŋ] as a salient variant, consistent with the Mongolic-derived lexical layer (Efimov 1965). ENGINE LIMIT: Efimov's claim of full /ŋ/ phonemicity in Mongolic loans cannot be expressed as a new independent phoneme without a dedicated grapheme in the Perso-Arabic base orthography (which has no letter for ŋ), so it stays a conditioned allophone of /n/, consistent with how fa-AF already encodes it.
